topic.title: No Visual Differences Detected
topic.shortdesc: Learn why the visual comparison tool may report no visible differences even when the source files differ.

keywords.indexterm: No visual differences between the two files were detected

body.p: When you use the file comparison tool in , the text versions of two files may differ even when you see one of the following messages: No visual differences between the two files were detected or There are differences that cannot be displayed in the visual comparison mode. This means that text mode would detect a difference, but no visible difference appears when the files are rendered in the visual comparison tool. In these cases, the differences are in the XML source and do not affect how the document looks in the visual editor or in the published output.

Possible scenarios include:
Whitespace Differences - The files could differ in the formatting or indentation of insignificant whitespace in the XML source. This whitespace exists only for readability in text mode and is not rendered in visual mode or in the output. For example, blank lines in the XML source are considered insignificant whitespace. If one file has more blank lines than the other, no visual differences are detected even though the text versions of the documents have a different number of lines. Another example is a difference in XML tag indentation.
Encoding Differences - If the two files use different encodings, there are no visual differences unless the encodings render characters differently.
Attribute Order Differences - If the two files differ only in the order of attributes within an element, and the attributes and elements are otherwise the same, visual mode does not detect any differences.
DOCTYPE Declaration Differences - If the two files differ in their DOCTYPE declaration, that difference is not detected in the visual comparison.
XML Comment Differences - If an XML comment is added inside an element that is not rendered in the visual editor or the output, this type of difference is not detected in the visual comparison. For example, this occurs when an XML comment is added between row elements within a table body element.
